findings.source_quote: ἐξεταστέον μή τις αὐτὸν μόνον ἀγαθὸν ὄντα ἐπὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς κακοῖς ὑπέβαλεν.
findings.english_quote: It must be examined whether someone has subjected him, though he is nothing but good, to all the evil things.
findings.issue: The material ambiguity in ὑπέβαλεν with ἐπὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς κακοῖς is insufficiently disclosed. The English can suggest making God undergo evils, whereas a false-presentation or imputation reading implicates him in the evils alleged against him. The preceding discussion of publicly written accusations makes that alternative particularly relevant. The note mentions accusations and representations as lexical possibilities, but does not supply this alternative construction or explain why subjection was selected. The main wording is defensible if understood as subjection to the adverse allegations; the problem is the unexplained choice between materially different meanings, not an unreadable or unverified source.
findings.suggested_revision: Explain explicitly whether 'subjected him … to all the evil things' means exposure to allegations or actual subjection to evils, and give the contextual reason for that choice. Preserve an attribution alternative in the note, such as 'It must be examined whether someone has falsely implicated him, though he is nothing but good, in all the evils.' Compare that candidate with the current wording before selecting the revised main text. Any replacement requires fresh review.
